name: gemma4-dev
description: Claude Code plugins for Google Cloud TPU DevOps: one management skill and one MCP server per Gemma 4 serving rig (JAX, PyTorch/torch_xla). Both are named after the rig directory — skill <rig>-management, tools prefixed mcp__<rig>__.

plugins.name: gce-jaxrust-v6e1-2b
plugins.description: Manage Google Cloud TPU capacity and Gemma 4 serving from Rust on Compute Engine TPU VMs: flex-start provisioning, capacity probing, quotas, cost estimates, and SRE diagnostics via the gce-jaxrust-v6e1-2b MCP server. The engine is Rust — rlx's JAX-shaped IR lowered to HLO and executed through libtpu's PJRT plugin, no Python in the serving path. Forked from tpu-jax-v6e1-2b 2026-08-28; nothing provisioned or measured on this path yet.

plugins.name: gce-pytorch-v6e1-2b
plugins.description: Compute Engine DevOps for the PyTorch/XLA Gemma 4 E2B rig: flex-start ct6e-standard-1t provisioning, capacity probing, quotas, cost estimates, and SRE diagnostics via the gce-pytorch-v6e1-2b MCP server. Serves google/gemma-4-E2B-it on one TPU v6e chip through public torch_xla (device "xla"), with the xprof + tensorboard profiling kit installed at boot. Forked from tpu-pytorch-v6e1-2b 2026-08-29 and migrated off the Cloud TPU API onto gcloud compute instances.

plugins.name: gpu-jax-g4dn-2b
plugins.description: EC2 G4dn DevOps for the pure-JAX Gemma 4 E2B rig: instance lifecycle, G-family quotas, x86_64 GPU DLAMI resolution, JAX-on-Turing verification, and SRE diagnostics via the gpu-jax-g4dn-2b MCP server. Serves google/gemma-4-E2B-it on an NVIDIA T4 (Turing, SM 7.5, 15360 MiB measured). Forked from gpu-jax-g5g-2b 2026-08-28 as the A/B control that separates Turing from Graviton2, and first served 2026-08-29: decode 13.1 tok/s against the T4G's 13.10, weight bytes identical to the byte, and the xprof profile reproducing 54.4% dtype conversion / 32.8% fp32 GEMV / 0.0% TensorCore — so the sibling's dtype tax is a chip finding, not a host one.

plugins.name: gpu-jax-g5g-2b
plugins.description: EC2 G5g DevOps for the pure-JAX Gemma 4 E2B rig: instance lifecycle, G-family quotas, arm64 GPU DLAMI resolution, JAX-on-Turing verification, and SRE diagnostics via the gpu-jax-g5g-2b MCP server. Serves google/gemma-4-E2B-it on an NVIDIA T4G (Turing, SM 7.5) behind an AWS Graviton2 host — no build, no CUDA toolkit, no Triton patch, because jax[cuda12] publishes aarch64 wheels that already carry sm_75.

plugins.name: gpu-jax-g6-2b
plugins.description: EC2 G6 DevOps for the pure-JAX Gemma 4 E2B rig: instance lifecycle, G-family quotas, x86_64 GPU DLAMI resolution, JAX-on-Ada verification, and SRE diagnostics via the gpu-jax-g6-2b MCP server. Serves google/gemma-4-E2B-it on an NVIDIA L4 (Ada, SM 8.9, 23034 MiB). Forked from gpu-jax-g5g-2b 2026-08-28 to move the same engine off Turing onto a native bfloat16 datapath: measured the same day at 48.3-48.5 tok/s against the T4G's 12.80 at an identical config, with the 54% dtype-conversion tax at 0.0% and decode at the bandwidth roofline.

plugins.name: gpu-jaxrust-g5g-2b
plugins.description: EC2 G5g DevOps for the Rust-driven-XLA Gemma 4 E2B rig: instance lifecycle, G-family quotas, arm64 GPU DLAMI resolution, Turing verification, and SRE diagnostics via the gpu-jaxrust-g5g-2b MCP server. Forked from gpu-jax-g5g-2b 2026-08-28 to move the engine off CPython onto Rust. The control plane is complete and measured nothing yet — the Rust engine is not written, and the rig currently runs the inherited Python JAX engine as its fallback and parity oracle.

plugins.name: gpu-llamacpp-g5g-2b-q4_0
plugins.description: EC2 G5g DevOps for the llama.cpp Gemma 4 E2B rig serving the QAT Q4_0 GGUF: instance lifecycle, G-family quotas, arm64 GPU DLAMI resolution, from-source llama.cpp build pinned to CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=75, and SRE diagnostics via the gpu-llamacpp-g5g-2b-q4_0 MCP server. Serves google/gemma-4-E2B-it-qat-q4_0-gguf on an NVIDIA T4G (Turing, SM 7.5) behind a Graviton2 host. Scaffolded 2026-09-02 and HAS SERVED NOTHING. The only rig here serving 4-bit weights on a GPU: vLLM 0.26.0 has no gguf module on any platform, no GGUF reader exists in JAX, and transformers dequantizes to fp32 while silently dropping 35 layer_scalar tensors. It compiles because llama.cpp publishes no prebuilt Linux aarch64 CUDA binary — the asymmetry against its gpu-ollama-g5g-2b-q4_0 sibling, which ships one with native sm_75 SASS.

plugins.name: gpu-ollama-g5g-2b-q4_0
plugins.description: EC2 G5g DevOps for the Ollama Gemma 4 E2B rig serving the QAT Q4_0 weights: instance lifecycle, G-family quotas, arm64 GPU DLAMI resolution, Ollama bundle install with the CUDA variant pinned to cuda_v12, and SRE diagnostics via the gpu-ollama-g5g-2b-q4_0 MCP server. Serves gemma4:e2b-it-qat on an NVIDIA T4G (Turing, SM 7.5) behind a Graviton2 host. Created 2026-09-02 and HAS SERVED NOTHING. Shares an engine with gpu-llamacpp-g5g-2b-q4_0 — Ollama links libllama.so — so slot 2 names the front end, not the decoder; the pair exists for the four differences a benchmark can still see. No build step: Ollama ships an aarch64 CUDA bundle with native sm_75 SASS where llama.cpp publishes none. Its failure mode is a CPU-resident model, which serves correctly and slowly and logs nothing, so the rig asserts on size_vram from /api/ps.

plugins.name: gpu-pytorch-g4dn-2b
plugins.description: EC2 G4dn DevOps for the PyTorch/transformers Gemma 4 E2B rig: instance lifecycle, G-family quotas, x86_64 PyTorch DLAMI resolution, torch-on-Turing verification, and SRE diagnostics via the gpu-pytorch-g4dn-2b MCP server. Serves google/gemma-4-E2B-it on an NVIDIA T4 (Turing, SM 7.5, 15360 MiB, 14.07 GiB usable). Forked from gpu-pytorch-g5g-2b 2026-08-29 as the fourth corner of the {jax, pytorch} x {g5g, g4dn} square. HAS SERVED NOTHING. Torch comes from the AMI rather than pip — the bootstrap installs into the DLAMI's own venv — so the image is a PyTorch DLAMI (2.13 / Ubuntu 26.04) and not the base driver image the JAX rigs use. Now that gpu-jax-g4dn-2b has closed the host axis, this is the runtime A/B on identical hardware: is the 86.9% dtype-plus-fp32-GEMV tax Turing, or XLA?

plugins.name: gpu-pytorch-g6-2b
plugins.description: EC2 G6 DevOps for the stock-PyTorch Gemma 4 E2B rig: instance lifecycle, G-family quotas, x86_64 PyTorch DLAMI resolution, torch-on-Ada verification, and SRE diagnostics via the gpu-pytorch-g6-2b MCP server. Serves google/gemma-4-E2B-it on an NVIDIA L4 (Ada, SM 8.9, 23034 MiB) through HF transformers -- no custom port, no XLA, no build. Retargeted from gpu-pytorch-g5g-2b 2026-08-29 and measured the same day at 20.93 tok/s, a clean 1.92x over the T4G at byte-identical weights. Sits at 71% of the bandwidth roofline where the JAX rig on the same chip reaches 99%: the gap is eager-mode kernel-launch overhead, and batching is untried.

plugins.name: gpu-vllm-g5g-2b
plugins.description: EC2 G5g DevOps for the vLLM Gemma 4 E2B rig: instance lifecycle, G-family quotas, arm64 AMI resolution, SM 7.5 build orchestration, and SRE diagnostics via the gpu-vllm-g5g-2b MCP server. Serves google/gemma-4-E2B-it on an NVIDIA T4G (Turing) behind an AWS Graviton2 host — the one rig here whose GPU has no prebuilt aarch64 CUDA kernels.

plugins.name: gpu-vllm-g6-2b
plugins.description: EC2 G6 DevOps for the vLLM Gemma 4 E2B rig: instance lifecycle, G-family quotas, x86_64 GPU DLAMI resolution, SM 8.9 verification, and SRE diagnostics via the gpu-vllm-g6-2b MCP server. Serves google/gemma-4-E2B-it on an NVIDIA L4 (Ada, SM 8.9). Forked from gpu-vllm-g5g-2b 2026-08-28, and the fork REMOVES that rig's reason for existing: G6 is x86_64 and SM 8.9, both carried by the published amd64 image, so there is no from-source build, no CUDA toolkit, no Rust and no Triton patch. Exists as the runtime control for gpu-jax-g6-2b on identical silicon. Has served nothing.

plugins.name: gpu-vllm-mi300x-2b
plugins.description: AMD MI300X DevOps for the vLLM Gemma 4 E2B rig: DigitalOcean droplet lifecycle (no create/destroy, by design), rocm-smi diagnostics that parse output rather than trust an exit code, image vetting that catches the newest vendor build being unable to load Gemma 4 at all, serving deployment with the gemma4 reasoning and tool-call parsers, and text/thinking/tool-calling/vision verification via the gpu-vllm-mi300x-2b MCP server. Serves google/gemma-4-E2B-it on one Instinct MI300X (gfx942, 191.69 GiB) reached through AMD Developer Cloud. The first AMD rig in this monorepo; added 2026-09-16.

plugins.name: gpu-vllm-t4-2b
plugins.description: Compute Engine DevOps for the vLLM Gemma 4 E2B rig on one already-attached NVIDIA Tesla T4 (Turing, SM 7.5, 15360 MiB): host capacity arithmetic across three filesystems, GPU architecture verification against the target interpreter, the Triton shared-memory clamp Turing needs, server lifecycle and SRE diagnostics via the gpu-vllm-t4-2b MCP server. Serves google/gemma-4-E2B-it-qat-w4a16-ct by default, with the bf16 reference kept for the A/B against gpu-vllm-g4dn-2b — same TU104 T4 at the same clocks, one rig provisioning its hardware and the other simply having it. The first gpu rig here with no provisioning half: no launch, no image resolution, no teardown. Measured 2026-09-18 — QAT decodes 1.79x bf16 per stream.

plugins.name: tpu-jax-v5e1-2b
plugins.description: TPU DevOps for the pure-JAX Gemma 4 rig: provisioning, queued resources, quotas, cost estimates, benchmarking, and SRE diagnostics via the tpu-jax-v5e1-2b MCP server. Serves google/gemma-4-E2B-it-qat-w4a16-ct on v5e-1 with no Docker and no HF token.

plugins.name: tpu-jax-v6e1-2b
plugins.description: Manage Google Cloud TPU capacity and Gemma 4 JAX serving on Compute Engine TPU VMs: flex-start provisioning, capacity probing, quotas, cost estimates, benchmarking, and SRE diagnostics via the tpu-jax-v6e1-2b MCP server.

plugins.name: tpu-pytorch-v5e1-12b
plugins.description: TPU DevOps for the PyTorch/torch_xla Gemma 4 12B rig: provisioning, queued resources, quotas, cost estimates, benchmarking, and SRE diagnostics via the tpu-pytorch-v5e1-12b MCP server. Static-shape decode server on v5e-1.
